issues.description: setuptools<82 cap leaked into runtime install_requires, not just CI
issues.detail: The CI scripts pinning setuptools<82 is a localized workaround for a build-time issue in mmcv. But adding 'setuptools<82' to core/setup.py's install_requires complects a transient CI/build problem with the runtime dependency contract of every downstream consumer of autogluon.core. Setuptools is a build tool, not a runtime value the program reasons about. This entangles 'what this package needs to install' with 'what some upstream package needs to build in our CI,' and the constraint will be silently inherited by every user forever.

issues.description: Two FIXME references to the same upstream issue, no single source of truth
issues.detail: The same upstream bug (mmcv#3325) is referenced in env_setup.sh, setup_mmcv.sh, and implicitly in core/setup.py (no comment there at all). When the upstream fix lands, three places must be reverted in sync, and the core/setup.py pin has no breadcrumb tying it to the cause. The fact that needs to be tracked ('we are pinning setuptools because of mmcv#3325') is a single value, but it has been duplicated and partially lost across files.

issues.description: mmdet version bumped from 3.2.0 to 3.3.0 inside an unrelated CI fix
issues.detail: The PR is titled 'Fix mmengine failure' but also silently bumps mmdet 3.2.0 -> 3.3.0. That is a separate change with separate risk surface, complected into a build-system workaround commit. Two concerns, one commit; if a regression appears, bisection cannot separate the mmdet bump from the setuptools cap.

Switching mmcv install to --no-build-isolation means the build now reads from the ambient environment's setuptools instead of an isolated one. This is the place-oriented escape hatch: the build's outcome now depends on global mutable state (which setuptools happens to be installed where) rather than a declared, isolated value. It works, but it makes the build less reproducible and more dependent on ordering of pip commands in the script.

issues.description: Removed pinned mmengine git SHA without recording why the torch 2.5 fix is no longer needed
issues.detail: The previous code installed mmengine from a specific git SHA 'with the fix for torch 2.5.' The new code installs mmengine==0.10.7 from PyPI. Is 0.10.7 the released version that contains that fix? The comment is gone, so the fact that mattered ('we need a torch-2.5-compatible mmengine') is no longer represented anywhere in the file. The value was discarded along with the identity.

review.summary: This is an easy fix, not a simple one. The mmcv build chain needs pkg_resources, setuptools 82 removed it, so the team pinned setuptools<82 in three places to make the immediate failure go away. That is fine as triage. What complects concerns is leaking a build-time CI workaround into core/setup.py's runtime install_requires, where it becomes a forever-constraint on every downstream user for a problem they will never encounter. The PR also bundles an unrelated mmdet version bump, drops the comment explaining why a specific mmengine version is required, and introduces --no-build-isolation, which is place-oriented coupling to the ambient environment. The hammock question: did anyone ask whether the runtime package needs to know anything about mmcv's build-time setuptools needs? The answer is no, and that is the one line that should not have shipped.
